blocks.text: KING OF JUDAH · TWO KINGDOMS
Ahaziah. One year in Jerusalem, killed in Jehu's revolt.
REIGNEDi
1 year c. 842–841 BC (dates vary)
CAPITAL
Jerusalem
HOUSE
House of David 6th of 20 in Judah
VERDICT
✕ Did evil “and did evil in the sight of the LORD, as did the house of Ahab”
PROPHETS
None named
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS REHOBOAM → ZEDEKIAH
ACCESSION
How Ahaziah came to power
Chronicles says the people of Jerusalem made him king because raiders had killed all his older brothers. 2 Chronicles 22:1
SUCCESSION
The two kingdoms
THE VERDICT
How Scripture judges the reign
“and did evil in the sight of the LORD, as did the house of Ahab”
2 Kings 8:27 (KJV) →
“And he walked in the way of the house of Ahab”
2 Kings 8:27 (KJV) →
BUT ALSO

Chronicles says his destruction "was of God by coming to Joram", and that he was buried because he was "the son of Jehoshaphat, who sought the LORD with all his heart". 2 Chronicles 22:7 2 Chronicles 22:9
CHRONICLES GIVES IT AS
“Wherefore he did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab”
2 Chronicles 22:4 (KJV) →
JUDAH (THE SOUTH): 20 RULERS
✓ Did right ✕ Did evil ◐ Mixed ● No verdict formula
THE KINGDOM
Jerusalem and the places of the reign
Judah (the south) · tribe of Judah. Only places Scripture names are shown, each where the Atlas puts it.
EVENTS
Wars, works and turning points
UNDATED IN SCRIPTURE
THE NATION
What the nation did
He walked in the way of the house of Ahab, "for he was the son in law of the house of Ahab". 2 Kings 8:27
ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
ARAM (DAMASCUS)
Hazael
ISRAEL
Joram son of Ahab · Jehu
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE
OUTSIDE THE BIBLE · ABOUT 840 BC
The Tel Dan stele
TWO ACCOUNTS
Where Kings and Chronicles differ
Each ribbon joins the two accounts of one matter, passage to passage.
His age
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
How he died
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
When he began
2 KINGS
2 CHRONICLES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S NUMBERS
No years given
1 year (2 Kgs 8:26). Scripture gives lengths and cross-dates, never BC years.
THIELE, REVISED BY MCFALL (1991)
Shared rule with Jehoram, 842–841 BC
Printed form: 841; co-regency from 842 (PDF p. 19).
YOUNG (2005), REVISING THIELE
Printed form: 841 (p. 246 (Table 2)).
ALBRIGHT (1945)
Printed form: c. 842 (p. 21).
TRADITIONAL DATES (USSHER, 1658)
Shared rule with Jehoram, 886–885 BC
Printed form: 885–884 (p. 49 (scan leaf n29)).
Two reckonings: co-king and sole king
Geneva Bible notes (1599); Kimchi and Abarbanel (as reported by John Gill, 1748–63)
He was made king at twenty-two while his father lived, and confirmed at forty-two. John Gill rejected this as received "without any proof". 2 Kings 8:26 2 Chronicles 22:2 [75][111]
Forty-two years of his mother's dynasty
John Lightfoot (as reported by Jamieson, Fausset and Brown, 1871); Matthew Poole (1683–85)
Forty-two counts the years of the house of Omri, not his age. 2 Chronicles 22:2 [134][123]
A copyist confused two numeral letters
C. F. Keil (1872); J. R. Lumby (1887); John Gill; Pulpit Commentary (1881)
The Hebrew letters for 20 and 40 were confused; forty-two is impossible, since his father died at forty. 2 Chronicles 21:20 2 Chronicles 22:2 [32][102][89][111]
IN SCRIPTURE
Every passage
CHAPTERS · 5
2 Kings 8 2 Kings 9 2 Kings 10 2 Chronicles 21 2 Chronicles 22
PASSAGES · 5
2 Kings 8:24–29 2 Kings 9:16–29 2 Kings 10:12–14 2 Chronicles 21:17 2 Chronicles 22:1–9
WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not name Ahaziah's wife here; Zibiah of Beersheba is named later as the mother of his son Joash.
No prophet is said to have spoken to Ahaziah himself.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON
From the textChronicles also calls him Jehoahaz (as Jehoram's youngest son) and, once, Azariah. He is not Ahaziah son of Ahab, king of Israel. 2 Chronicles 21:17 2 Chronicles 22:1 2 Chronicles 22:6

links.text: Athaliah, Queen who reigned over Judah, 6 years
Ben-hadad, King of Syria (Aram), son of Hazael, Scripture gives no length of reign., c. 798 BC, no regnal verdict in Scripture
Omri, King of Israel, Twelve years, six of them in Tirzah (1 Kings 16:23), c. 885–874 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
Ahaziah, King of Israel, Two years (1 Kings 22:51), c. 853–852 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
Jehoash, King of Israel, Sixteen years (2 Kings 13:10), c. 798–782 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
Jeroboam II, King of Israel, Forty-one years in Samaria (2 Kings 14:23), c. 793–753 BC, did evil in the eyes of the LORD
